query: What business models and customers do these companies describe?

per_column.name: Business Model
per_column.rationale: Directly answers the 'business models' half of the query and provides a rich categorical axis (20 distinct categories) for grouping and comparison. Most samples are soundly derived: 23andMe->Life Sciences/Digital Health, 280 Group->Consulting, the two VC firms->Venture Capital. However Addepar, described as a 'performance reporting platform' for financial assets, was labeled 'Marketing / Ad Tech', which contradicts the source (should be Fintech/Financial Software). This mislabel indicates some values are not sound readings, lowering groundedness.

per_column.name: Primary Customer Segment
per_column.rationale: Directly addresses the 'customers' half of the query and gives a useful segmentation axis (B2B/B2C/Enterprise/Investors/etc.) to group companies on. Values in samples are well-warranted: 23andMe consumer reports->B2C, VC firms serving founders/investors->Investors/Founders, consulting->B2B. The heavy dominance of B2B is a reasonable inference for these tech companies rather than an invented specific; segments are clearly derivable from the descriptions.

judge.rationale: Both columns map cleanly onto the two facets of the analytical query (business model and customer type), each offering a genuine categorical axis for grouping and comparison rather than trivial restatements or generic metrics. Values are mostly sound extractions/categorisations of the company descriptions. The main groundedness weakness is at least one clearly wrong Business Model label (Addepar, a financial reporting platform, tagged Marketing/Ad Tech), indicating occasional unsupported categorisations; Customer Segment values are consistently defensible.
